Make sure that you do not miss this because this is about to be the biggest part of the entire Artemis mission and the footage that comes back from Monday is going to be absolutely insane. So happening on Monday, the Artemis crew is going to be flying behind the moon and this is everything that is about to happen. They are going to pass 4,700 miles from the far side of the moon, which will officially make them the farthest humans from earth in all of recorded history. During a six hour window they're going to be photographing craters from the far side of the moon that no human being has actually ever been able to see before with their own eyes. NASA has already been planning which exact spots that they're going to be shooting and the crew has been setting up camera lenses all week so they're ready for this moment. Whenever the Artemis crew is behind the moon they are going to be losing all communication with Earth for about 40 minutes. No signal, no mission control, completely alone out there without any communication. And during that blackout, they are going to be seeing a solar eclipse. Earth is going to be crossing in front of the sun from their view, creating a solar eclipse that nobody's ever been able to witness

from that angle ever in history. Guys, this is about to be insane. Make sure that you go ahead and add me right now if you're watching this video because I'm going to be showing you every single photo, every single clip, and every single piece of footage the second it comes back. Monday is two days away.
